hooks.text: Soviet orbital satellites once confirmed an incoming nuclear strike with highest reliability.
A satellite once mistook high-altitude clouds for incoming American nuclear missiles.
Why did glinting sunlight on clouds almost trigger World War Three?

title: The 25-Minute Countdown That Almost Ended the World
description: In September 1983, a Soviet early-warning satellite detected incoming American nuclear missiles. Duty officer Stanislav Petrov had minutes to decide whether to trigger World War Three.

beats.text: Soviet orbital satellites once confirmed an incoming nuclear strike with highest reliability.
beats.visual: illustration of Soviet Oko nuclear early-warning satellite orbiting Earth, 1983

beats.text: On September 26, 1983, early-warning screens alerted duty officer Stanislav Petrov to five American missiles.
beats.visual: portrait photograph of Soviet duty officer Stanislav Petrov in military uniform

beats.text: With impact minutes away, computers insisted an attack was underway.
beats.visual: photograph of an American Minuteman intercontinental ballistic missile launching from an underground silo

beats.text: Yet Petrov suspected a real American strike would be an overwhelming barrage, not five isolated launches.
beats.visual: photograph of Stanislav Petrov seated at a military monitoring desk

beats.text: Ground radar showed clear skies, confirming his suspicion.
beats.visual: photograph of a massive Cold War over-the-horizon radar installation antenna array

beats.text: Petrov decided against reporting an attack, alerting headquarters instead that the system had malfunctioned.
beats.visual: portrait photograph of Stanislav Petrov in front of military monitors

beats.text: Investigations revealed satellites encountered a rare solar alignment.
beats.visual: diagram illustrating the orbital path of a Soviet early-warning satellite relative to the Sun

beats.text: Blinded by the glare, the sensors mistook sunlight reflecting off high-altitude clouds for missile launches.
beats.visual: satellite photograph of brilliant sunlight glinting off high-altitude Earth clouds from orbit

beats.text: Glinting sunlight bouncing off clouds had triggered humanity's closest nuclear false alarm.
beats.visual: portrait photograph of Stanislav Petrov in later years holding an award

better_than_last: Delays the hazard resolution until the final beats and establishes an immediate high-stakes contradiction hook to maximize viewer retention.
